decisions.reason: The source establishes copy specifically for the coded-referral Mint successful modal; it does not request any landing-page copy or layout change.
The modal-specific wording does not change the About page's content, topics, or unresolved prize-payout description.
The client assigns the new wording only to the Mint successful modal and does not revise the FAQ or establish a global commission-copy change.
The source applies whenever a referral code is used, whereas this candidate governs commission allocation when a code is missing or invalid.

The source proposes modal wording containing '$12 commission' but does not explicitly change the on-chain mint-price allocation or affiliate commission amount; propagating a revenue-split change would require a separate client decision.
The coded-referral success message does not alter whether prizes are transferred automatically or claimed through a control.
The source changes success-modal text and has no effect on the landing-page book cover's placement, size, or cropping.
The modal copy applies after a coded-referral mint but does not change the USDC payment, approval, or mint-execution behavior.
The source does not change the fiat provider, wallet provisioning, supported payment methods, mint destination, or deferred lifecycle of Transak minting.
The coded-referral success copy does not affect optional gratuity amounts, tip processing, or the delayed follow-up notice.
The success-modal wording does not alter the NFT ebook format or unlimited edition supply.
The source changes coded-referral feedback copy only and does not alter ETH pricing, swap execution, shortfall handling, or excess-refund behavior.
